text.p: DuPont Packaging and Industrial Polymers said Monday that it has completed the sale of its "Alcryn" brand of melt processible rubber to a private investment group effective May 30.
Terms of the sale are not disclosed.

"Alcryn," introduced by the DuPont Co unit in 1986, has grown steadily as a specialized thermoplastic elastomer (TPE) serving automotive and other markets. It is made using proprietary DuPont resins which DuPont will continue to supply to the new owners -- a newly formed Wilmington company named Advanced Polymer Alloys Inc.

Packaging and Industrial Polymers exlained "Alcryn" is a good product in the marketplace; however, DuPont's focus is on other businesses core to future growth. Sale of 'Alcryn' helps assure that the product will receive the attention needed for its own continued growth and success.
It said the investment group buying the business will employ former DuPont personnel who had been responsible for "Alcryn" manufacturing and marketing.

The sale includes rights to the "Alcryn" tradename and remaining patent protection. The new owners will operate the "Alcryn" business worldwide, with the exception of Japan, where a Mitsui-DuPont joint venture will support local customers.
